# EG Plan Model v1: coach review

**What it does.** A friend answers 12 questions (goal, height, weight, age, sex, training history, push-up and squat counts, barbell experience, days, minutes, equipment, focus areas, areas to go easy on, and a health question). The model turns those into an 8-week plan picked from the app’s 5,632-exercise catalogue, with a short explanation for each choice. Every number below comes from these tables; nothing is generated by AI.

**What it does not do.** It does not diagnose, rehabilitate, or plan around medical conditions: a health answer of yes stops it and suggests a doctor or physiotherapist. It does not change a plan by itself after it starts; the app’s usual double progression moves weights within the plan’s rep ranges.
**What we ask you.** Check the tables, the core exercise list and the three worked plans. Anything you would change, write it down with the reason. Until you sign off, plans show "Not reviewed by a coach yet".

## 1. Who the person is

- **Level:** never trained or under 6 months = novice; 6 months to 2 years = intermediate; over 2 years = advanced. Under 6 months plus 11+ push-ups, 11+ squats and barbell experience = intermediate.
- **Body:** BMI bands (under 18.5, 18.5 to 25, 25 to 30, over 30) only steer emphasis: a lean person gaining gets compound-first wording; BMI 25+ with fat-loss goals keeps heavy lifting and adds easy cardio or steps. Never shown as a label.
- **Age 50+:** one set fewer in weeks 1 and 2, +30 s rest on compound lifts.
- **Sex:** a woman with no focus picked gets glutes and legs as default focus (one more set or slot), isolation rests of 60 s instead of 75 s, and one more accessory set where time allows. "Prefer not to say" uses the neutral defaults. Safety rules never differ.

## 2. Splits and sessions

| Days | Novice | Intermediate | Advanced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | Full body A, Full body B | Full body A, Full body B | Full body A, Full body B |
| 3 | Full body A, Full body B, Full body C | Upper A, Lower A, Full body B | Upper A, Lower A, Full body B |
| 4 | Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B | Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B | Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B |
| 5 | Upper A, Lower A, Full body A, Upper B, Lower B | Upper A, Lower A, Push, Pull, Legs | Upper A, Lower A, Push, Pull, Legs |

| Session | Slots in order (M = main lift, A = accessory) |
| --- | --- |
| Full body A | M squat, M hpush, M hpull, A hipext, A latraise, A core |
| Full body B | M hinge, M vpush, M vpull, A hpush, A lunge, A curl |
| Full body C | M squat, M hpush, M hpull, A kneeflex, A reardelt, A corerot |
| Upper A | M hpush, M hpull, M vpush, M vpull, A latraise, A curl, A triext |
| Upper B | M vpull, M hpush, M hpull, M vpush, A fly, A reardelt, A triext, A curl |
| Lower A | M squat, M hinge, A lunge, A kneeflex, A calf, A core |
| Lower B | M hinge, M squat, A hipext, A kneeext, A calf, A corerot |
| Push | M hpush, M vpush, A hpush, A latraise, A fly, A triext |
| Pull | M vpull, M hpull, A hpull, A reardelt, A curl, A curl |
| Legs | M squat, M hinge, A lunge, A kneeflex, A kneeext, A calf |

Focus areas add one accessory slot (or a set to an existing one) in the first session training that area: chest → fly, back → hpull, shoulders → latraise, arms → curl, glutes → hipext, legs → lunge, core → core. Sessions are trimmed to the minutes chosen (estimate: 8 min warm-up, 40 s per set, the prescribed rests): extras whose muscles are already covered go first, then fourth sets, then other extras. A novice gaining weight or strength keeps at most 1 isolation exercise per session.

| hybrid | 5 to 8 | 8 to 12 | 10 to 15 |

Novice strength main lifts: 5 to 8. Core work: 10 to 15 reps, holds 20 to 40 s (novice) or 30 to 60 s.

| Phase | Novice (main / accessory RIR) | Intermediate | Advanced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Weeks 1 to 2 | 3 / 4 | 3 / 2 | 2 / 2 |
| Weeks 3 to 7 | 2 / 2 | 2 / 1 | 2 / 1 |
| Week 8 | one set fewer, +1 RIR | same | same |

Strength emphasis keeps main lifts at RIR 2. Novices and over-50s start weeks 1 to 2 one set lower.

| Exercise type | Rest |
| --- | --- |
| Main lift | 2:30 |
| Main lift, strength emphasis | 3:00 |
| Compound accessory | 2:00 |
| Isolation and core | 1:15 |
| Isolation, female profile | 1:00 |

Cardio (fat loss, strength and cardio, or general with BMI 25+): two easy 20-minute blocks (25 for strength and cardio) at the end of sessions when they fit, otherwise a daily 8,000 to 10,000 steps note.

## 4. Choosing exercises

For each slot the model scores every eligible exercise of that movement pattern and takes the best. It may only use equipment the person has, never an exercise that loads an area they asked to go easy on, and for main lifts only the core list below, at a skill no more than one step above their level (novice: machines and supported moves; intermediate: free weights; advanced: barbell compounds).
| Score | Points |
| --- | --- |
| core | 30 |
| common | 10 |
| variant | 0 |
| compound | 15 |
| skillFit | 10 |
| familiar | 10 |
| favourite | 10 |
| repeatEquipPattern | -20 |
| repeatInSession | -40 |
| jitter | 4 |

## 5. Worked plans

### Friend A: 176 cm, 75 kg, male, trains 6 months to 2 years, strong; muscle and fat loss, 4 days, 60 min, full gym
**Your plan: muscle and fat loss, 4 days.** Sessions about 35 to 65 min.

Why, as the person sees it:
- You have trained regularly for a while, so the plan uses more sets and works closer to your limit.
- An upper and lower split: each muscle is trained twice a week, and each session has room for both heavy lifts and smaller exercises.
- Moderate reps close to your limit keep and build muscle while you lose fat.
- After two easier weeks you work 1 to 2 reps short of your limit, close enough to build muscle without grinding every set.
- Longer rests on the big lifts (about 2 to 3 minutes) protect the quality of the next set; smaller exercises need about a minute.
- There is no time left in the sessions for cardio, so aim for 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day instead.
- To fit 60 minutes, the plan keeps the most useful exercises and drops the extras.
- Eight weeks: two easier weeks to find your weights, five full weeks where the app moves your weights up as you hit the top of the rep range, and a lighter last week.

### Friend B: 187 cm, 68 kg, male, new to the gym; gain weight and muscle, 3 days, 60 min, full gym
**Your plan: weight and muscle, 3 days.** Sessions about 30 to 55 min.

Why, as the person sees it:
- You are new to regular training, so the plan builds technique and confidence first.
- You are lean for your height and want to gain, so the plan leans on big compound lifts that add the most muscle.
- As a newcomer looking to gain, most of your time goes to big compound lifts, with just one smaller exercise per session.
- 3 full-body days: every muscle gets trained 3 times a week with a few sets each time, which suits someone new to training and builds the main lifts fastest.
- 6 to 10 reps on big compound lifts add the most muscle and weight for the time you spend.
- The first two weeks stop 3 to 4 reps short of your limit while you learn the lifts; from week 3 you work about 2 reps short.
- Longer rests on the big lifts (about 2 to 3 minutes) protect the quality of the next set; smaller exercises need about a minute.
- Eight weeks: two easier weeks to find your weights, five full weeks where the app moves your weights up as you hit the top of the rep range, and a lighter last week.
